reviewRequestsUpdate.title: B. Era and the phone
reviewRequestsUpdate.userAnswer: It was written in the flip phone era [...] / Update all cellphones to smart phones.
reviewRequestsUpdate.decision: Present day. Every cell phone in the film is a smartphone: the blocked-number displays (100, 248, 295), the call gone at 265 and the split screen (1690) are smartphone screens; the television at 1534 is a flat screen. Line 818's phone slammed shut is staged as a hard end-call and the phone thrown to the passenger seat (the writer's staging, no line changes). The writer's default (period-neutral with a hinge phone) is withdrawn.

reviewRequestsUpdate.title: K. The agency
reviewRequestsUpdate.userAnswer: AI really doesn't know what difference between fed and statie? [...] / It's just state police and federal agents. / Switch it to FBI / Idk bout the cops would AI know what MA State Police look like / For uniformed cops
reviewRequestsUpdate.decision: The Massachusetts State Police is the agency of John, Diego, the captain and every uniformed officer (the script's State police at 525 and 1809). The two agents are FBI, as the script already names them at 334 and 1764; the writer reads 'Switch it to FBI' as correcting the question's wording ('a federal case'), so nothing in the script changes. PD, precinct and barracks in the script are the author's colloquial words for the same agency and never appear on signage. The writer's default is confirmed for John, Diego, the captain and the uniforms; the federal side is named FBI by the author; his 'Idk bout the cops' is a doubt whether the model can render the agency's look, answered in scope.

reviewRequestsUpdate.title: O. Screen length (for Ziggy and Baldadoon together)
reviewRequestsUpdate.userAnswer: That last part what is it asking? [...] / Oh, like is it a show or a movie / Single film. (Between the two questions Ziggy glossed O as estimated run time, whether it is meant to be one, or maybe multiple parts.)
reviewRequestsUpdate.decision: The whole screenplay as one film, as the writer reads 'Single film' against Ziggy's gloss (one or multiple parts; show or movie). The question's second option, a contained excerpt first, was not put to the author in those words, so the site card's scope question is answered in substance and closed by the one-line follow-up O-f1.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: S. John's car (the author's instruction, given unasked with his answer to K)
reviewRequestsAppend.question: Not asked by the writer. The author added it while answering K; Ziggy then asked him whether the police cars were the older full-size sedans.
reviewRequestsAppend.userAnswer: The cop car needs to be an unmarked dodge charger. Cops don't use the brand I wrote any more / (to Ziggy's question whether the police cars were the older full-size sedans:) Not anymore they all got them suvs / Midwest got durangos and pick ups [...]
reviewRequestsAppend.decision: John's unmarked car is a present-day Dodge Charger; the author's instruction replaces the Chevy Impala of line 96. The brand appears in the writer's record only; every provider-facing text keeps 'a dark unmarked sedan'. The author's SUV remarks answered a general question about police cars; the writer applies them to the marked vehicles (present-day SUVs) and keeps John in the sedan the author named (S-f1 asks the one word if he meant otherwise). The set family keeps TCM-SET-IMPALA as its working id.

reviewRequestsAppend.title: B-f1. Can the calls be traced in the present day?
reviewRequestsAppend.question: B-f1 (the author's own remark, 'Only issue is what brand can he have that has actual privacy', which the writer reads as being about the phone; the author corrects the reading if it was about the car): in the present day, does the script need a reason on screen why the calls cannot be traced (the trace attempts at 388 and 1291 fail as written), or does it stand as written? No brand is named on screen either way. Question A (does the phone really ring) bears on it; the writer does not repair the plot.
reviewRequestsAppend.writerDefault: as written; no brand on screen

reviewRequestsAppend.title: O-f1. The whole screenplay, not an excerpt first?
reviewRequestsAppend.question: O-f1 (one word): the whole screenplay as the one film, rather than a contained excerpt made first as a proof? The writer proceeds on the whole screenplay unless the author says excerpt.
